extracted.intended_audience: Ballotpedia readers, voters, and researchers seeking information on fact-checking organizations
extracted.subtask_description: A concise encyclopedic summary of PolitiFact's mission, how it selects claims to check, and the Truth-o-Meter rating scale it uses to judge statements. Also notes its nonpartisan editorial stance and organizational affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: focus on specific statements by politicians
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact says that it is focuses "on looking at specific statements made by politicians and rating them for accuracy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the site's topical scope — items checked are discrete claims attributable to political actors rather than broad analysis or opinion pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim selection process / newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Each day, PolitiFact journalists look for statements to fact-check. We read transcripts, speeches, news stories, press releases, and campaign brochures. We watch TV and scan social media. Readers send us suggestions via email to truthometer@politifact.com; we often fact-check statements submitted by readers. Because we can't feasibly check all claims, we select the most newsworthy and significant ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources and inputs for selecting claims: transcripts, speeches, news stories, press releases, campaign brochures, TV, social media, and reader submissions. Selection is constrained by capacity; priority is given to claims judged 'newsworthy' and 'significant.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth-o-Meter accuracy scale
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact developed a Truth-o-Meter accuracy scale to judge claims. The scale runs from TRUE to PANTS ON FIRE, with four intermediate ratings that account for degrees of accuracy and missing context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scale is ordinal and designed to capture degrees of accuracy and contextual errors; the page references 'four intermediate ratings' (not enumerated here) and points to PolitiFact's Principles of the Truth-O-Meter for the detailed methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence and nonpartisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact describes itself as a "nonpartisan fact-checking website to sort out the truth in American politics." It does not take editorial positions or endorse candidates or policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a stated normative standard guiding PolitiFact's work: maintain nonpartisanship, avoid editorial endorsements, and present findings as independent fact-checks.
